messages:
alex: Heads-up — I have a small repro where Retrofit (suspend) + OkHttp Authenticator + WorkManager ends up triggering duplicate token refreshes and occasional 401 loops on Pixel 8 / Android 14.
leah: ugh. repro steps?
alex: Steps: 1) Worker (WorkManager) enqueues a suspend Retrofit call `api.getFoo()` 2) server responds 401 (token expired) 3) coroutine gets cancelled/retried by WorkManager -> sometimes see authenticator run twice for the same logical request. Minimal logs below.
alex: ```
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/foo
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 Unauthorized (token invalid)
I/OkHttp: Authenticator: refreshing token (start)
I/OkHttp: --> POST /v1/foo (with refreshed token)
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 Unauthorized
I/OkHttp: Authenticator: refreshing token (start) 
I/OkHttp: <-- 200 OK
```
ryan: is the authenticator being invoked for both the original and the follow-up network calls? could be that WorkManager retry/cancel creates a second call object.
leah: are you using the suspend CallAdapter that wraps `Call` in `suspendCancellableCoroutine`? if not cancellation may not propagate to OkHttp and leaves an in-flight call that still triggers the authenticator.
alex: yes using the kotlinx suspend adapter shipped by Retrofit. I did wrap it but saw we weren't canceling the underlying Call on coroutine cancel in our older helper.
eng-ci-bot: Reminder: please attach reproducible sample and stack trace when filing.
ryan: quick thought: OkHttp's Authenticator can be invoked by follow-up requests created internally; if the original coroutine is cancelled but the OkHttp follow-up continues, you can get two refresh attempts.
leah: short-term workaround: coalesce refreshes at the auth layer — track an in-flight refresh per account (AtomicReference / Mutex) and wait for it instead of starting a new one. Also log `call.hashCode()` / request id in EventListener to correlate calls.
alex: tried that; it reduced noise but still saw a narrow window where WorkManager re-enqueues the Worker, creating a fresh JVM coroutine while previous one still finalizing a follow-up call.
ryan: posted a draft SDK PR adding an optional `AuthenticatorCoalescing` helper and a `suspendCall` utility that cancels underlying OkHttp call on coroutine cancel. Link: https://github.com/redwood/sdk/pull/NNN
alex: the `suspendCall` change looks like this locally and fixed most repros: 
alex: ```kotlin
suspend fun <T> Call.awaitResponse(): Response<T> = suspendCancellableCoroutine { cont ->
  enqueue(object : Callback {
    override fun onResponse(call: Call, resp: Response) { cont.resume(resp) }
    override fun onFailure(call: Call, e: IOException) { cont.resumeWithException(e) }
  })
  cont.invokeOnCancellation { try { cancel() } catch (ignored: Throwable) {} }
}
```
leah: thats the known pattern. also ensure your Retrofit instance uses a single OkHttpClient across requests (no per-call clients) — creating clients can lead to surprising connection reuse semantics.
ryan: also experiment with `OkHttpClient.callTimeout(...)` and `Dispatcher` tuning so WorkManager's retry patterns don't leave long-lived calls.
alex: filing an issue with steps + repro app: https://storage.internal/repro/kotlin-okhttp-auth-cancel.zip. Will test your PR on device farm.
leah: follow-up: add idempotency key for POSTs where possible so duplicate retries are safe. and add jittered backoff on refresh to avoid thundering herd when WorkManager restarts.
ryan: thanks for the repro — I'll run it across Pixel farm and confirm. :thumbsup:
alex: thanks both, will push sample & logs to the issue.
